## Problem

A Total Rewards team asks questions that cross systems: are we paying within range, what do benefits cost per employee, does payroll tie to the ledger, does the carrier's file match HR? My [benefits reconciliation project](benefits-ledger.qmd) answers one of them, tying billing and payments to the ledger in Power BI. This project builds everything upstream of the report, so the numbers arrive tested and traceable.

::: {.origin}
The company, people and pay are invented. Northwind Mutual is fictional, and every record comes from a Python generator with a fixed seed.
:::

## The product

**Business questions it's being built to answer:** pay-range position (compa-ratio), benefits cost per employee, payroll-to-ledger tie-out, carrier file reconciliation, and a total rewards statement per employee.

**Planned pipeline:** HCM-style extract files and a mock API → Python ingestion → AWS S3, Glue and Athena → dbt models with automated data-quality tests → Power BI.

The generator is planned to reach about 2 million rows: hires, terms, rehires, retirees, salary history, benefit elections, payroll, 401(k), PTO and general ledger entries, with planted errors and an answer key to check them against.

**Built so far (Day 5):** a seeded generator that creates 25 fictional employees, each with a unique ID, a job from a [5-job catalog](https://github.com/analysttom712/total-rewards-analytics/blob/main/generator/job_catalog.py) and a salary inside that job's pay band, written to CSV with pandas. Three [pytest tests](https://github.com/analysttom712/total-rewards-analytics/blob/main/tests/test_generator.py) check that the output is reproducible, the employee IDs are unique and every salary sits inside its band. These are the same two checks I run on any census file before trusting it: no duplicate IDs, nobody paid outside their band.

**Guardrails:** [CI](https://github.com/analysttom712/total-rewards-analytics/blob/main/.github/workflows/checks.yml) runs a public-repo safety scan, ruff and pytest on every pull request, and a pre-commit hook runs the same scan before anything is committed. Claude built the CI and the scan (AI-assisted); learning to build CI myself is a later milestone.

## How it's run

I run it like a job on an agile team. Unlike my other projects, where AI wrote the code at my direction, here I write the first attempt myself, with hints and, when stuck, partial code, to learn it. Claude (AI) acts as my lead engineer: it writes the tickets and setup files, teaches each concept, gives hints and reviews my pull requests.

| Team practice | How it shows up here |
|---|---|
| Backlog | GitHub Issues written as business asks, with acceptance criteria, a learning objective and an estimate |
| Daily standup | Each session opens with yesterday, today's ticket and blockers |
| Definition of done | Checks pass, safety scan, pull request reviewed and merged, learning log updated, post drafted |
| Decision records | [ADR-001 to ADR-004](https://github.com/analysttom712/total-rewards-analytics/blob/main/docs/DECISIONS.md): job catalog as a constant, synthetic ID rules, rules enforced by tools instead of wording, one save at a time behind a lock |
| Sprints | Planned: two-week reviews: what shipped, skills update, next stretch goal |
| Incidents | Starting in M1: planned drills: the pipeline is broken on purpose; I troubleshoot, write a blameless postmortem and add a test that would have caught it |

## Why I'm building it

It turns my background in benefits, payroll and accounting reconciliation into engineering work an employer can inspect: every change and fix is in a public commit history.

## What the business should do

**Planned.** The platform is being built so a Total Rewards team can act each month on four checks: pay outside range, benefits cost per employee, payroll that doesn't tie to the ledger, and carrier files that don't match HR. The first piece exists: every generated salary is [tested against its pay band](https://github.com/analysttom712/total-rewards-analytics/blob/main/tests/test_generator.py). The recommendations come once the models do.
